Mox v0.9.0 adds native Arch Linux distribution and more confirmation keys,
improves empty-state guidance, and fixes connection status messages for
hostnames containing percent signs.

This is a minor release under Semantic Versioning: the additions preserve
existing commands and configuration formats.

### Terminal UI and commands

- Press `n` or `N` to cancel a kill confirmation, a delete confirmation,
  or an add-wizard draft discard. Kill and delete confirmations also
  accept uppercase `Y`.
- An empty `mox list` suggests `mox init` or `mox new`. When an editor
  filter has no matches, the detail pane explains how to clear the search.
- Session preview sanitization and table rendering avoid redundant ANSI
  scans and temporary allocations.

### Reliability

- Connection retry and hold messages treat hostnames as `printf` arguments.
  Percent signs, including those in IPv6 zone identifiers such as
  `fe80::1%eth0`, are displayed literally.
- Arch packaging restores the expected signing key and handles checkout
  ownership inside its build container.

### Arch Linux distribution

- Each release publishes native `mox-tmux` packages for x86_64 and aarch64,
  built from the same verified binaries as the Linux archives.
- Signed pacman repositories provide automatic updates without an AUR
  account or helper. Packages and repository databases are signed.
- See the [Arch installation guide](https://github.com/bthall/mox/blob/v0.9.0/docs/arch-linux.md)
  for package verification and repository setup. This distribution support
  was also backfilled for v0.8.0.

### Install or update

Download the archive for your OS and architecture below and verify it against
`checksums.txt`, or build the tagged version with Go 1.25 or newer:

```sh
go install github.com/bthall/mox/cmd/mox@v0.9.0
```

Runtime requires tmux 3.1 or newer. Existing configurations continue to work;
updating the binary does not require restarting running tmux sessions.
